title: Injective approximation with ideal-power torsion cokernel
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings, $\varphi:R\to S$ a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $t\in\mathbf N$, $f:\operatorname{Fin}(t)\to R$, and $I=(f_i)_i$, with $R/I\to S/IS$ bijective. Let $\mathrm{Can}:\mathrm{Mod}_R\to\mathrm{Glue}(\varphi,f)$ be a functor [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data] with prime module $S\otimes_R M$ [def-weil-module-base-change], chart modules $M_{f_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], and comparison and interchange maps the canonical ones for every $M$ (bundled equalities for the modules, heterogeneous equalities for the structural linear maps). All modules lie in universe $\max(u,v,w)$, where $R$ and $S$ lie in universes $u$ and $v$. For every datum $X$ there exist an $R$-module $H$ in that universe and a glueing morphism $\psi:\mathrm{Can}(H)\to X$ such that $\psi'$ is injective, each chart map $\psi_i$ is bijective, and every element $x$ of $Q=X.M'/\operatorname{im}\psi'$, regarded as an $R$-module through $\varphi$, has an integer $n\ge1$ with $I^n x=0$. This conclusion is an approximation; it does not assert that $\psi'$ is surjective.

proof.text: (Part (2): the module $H^0(\mathbf M)$ and the morphism $\Psi$.) Let $\mathbf M=(M',(M_i),(\alpha_i),(\alpha_{ij}))$ be an object of $\mathrm{Glue}$. Let $H=H^0(\mathbf M)\subseteq M'\times\prod_iM_i$ be the $R$-module of the families $(m',(m_i))$ with $\alpha_i(m'/1)=m_i\otimes1$ and $\alpha_{ij}(m_i/1)=m_j/1$ for all $i,j$, with projections $p':H\to M'$ and $p_i:H\to M_i$ (Remark 05EL). By [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-H0-localization] there is for each $i$ a unique $R$-linear $\Psi_i:H_{f_i}\to M_i$ with $\Psi_i(h/1)=p_i(h)$, and it is bijective; as $f_i$ acts bijectively on $M_i$, $\Psi_i(h/f_i^e)=f_i^{-e}p_i(h)$. Let $\Psi':H\otimes_RS\to M'$ be the $S$-linear map with $\Psi'(h\otimes s)=s\,p'(h)$ (well defined since $(h,s)\mapsto s\,p'(h)$ is $R$-bilinear [def-weil-module-base-change]). Then $\Psi=(\Psi',(\Psi_i)_i):\mathrm{Can}(H)\to\mathbf M$ is a morphism of $\mathrm{Glue}$ [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data]: (i) $\alpha_i\circ\Psi'_{f_i}=(\Psi_i\otimes_RS)\circ c^H_{f_i}$, since on $(h\otimes s)/f_i^e$ the left side is $\alpha_i(s\,p'(h)/f_i^e)=s f_i^{-e}\alpha_i(p'(h)/1)=sf_i^{-e}(p_i(h)\otimes1)$ ($\alpha_i$ is $S$-linear and $R$-linear) and the right side is $(\Psi_i\otimes_RS)((h/f_i^e)\otimes s)=f_i^{-e}p_i(h)\otimes s$, the same element; (ii) $\alpha_{ij}\circ(\Psi_i)_{f_j}=(\Psi_j)_{f_i}\circ\sigma^H_{f_i,f_j}$, since on $(h/f_i^a)/f_j^b$ the left side is $\alpha_{ij}((f_i^{-a}p_i(h))/f_j^b)=f_i^{-a}f_j^{-b}\alpha_{ij}(p_i(h)/1)=f_i^{-a}f_j^{-b}(p_j(h)/1)$ and the right side is $(\Psi_j)_{f_i}((h/f_j^b)/f_i^a)=(f_j^{-b}p_j(h))/f_i^a$, the same element ($\alpha_{ij}$ is $R$-linear between modules on which $f_i,f_j$ act bijectively, so it commutes with their inverses). These elements generate the sources additively (step 1), using the formulas for $c$ and $\sigma$ [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-canonical-maps]. Bundle H in the specified universe. Transport the component maps along the object identifications of Can; their heterogeneous structural-map equalities preserve the two morphism equations.

(Part (2): $\Psi'$ has $I$-power torsion kernel and cokernel.) By (i) of step 1, $\Psi'_{f_i}=\alpha_i^{-1}\circ(\Psi_i\otimes_RS)\circ c^H_{f_i}$, a composite of isomorphisms ($\alpha_i$ by [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data], $c^H_{f_i}$ by step 1, $\Psi_i\otimes_RS$ with inverse $\Psi_i^{-1}\otimes_RS$ [def-weil-module-base-change]). Let $K=\operatorname{Ker}\Psi'$ and $Q=\operatorname{Coker}\Psi'$, $S$-modules. Localizing the exact sequences of $R$-modules $0\to K\to H\otimes_RS\xrightarrow{\Psi'}M'$ and $H\otimes_RS\xrightarrow{\Psi'}M'\to Q\to0$ at $\{1,f_i,f_i^2,\dots\}$ gives exact sequences [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] in which $\Psi'_{f_i}$ is bijective, so $K_{f_i}=0$ and $Q_{f_i}=0$. For $x\in K$ (or $Q$), $x/1=0$ in $K_{f_i}$ gives $e_i$ with $f_i^{e_i}x=0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]; with $e=e_1+\dots+e_t$ every monomial $f_1^{a_1}\cdots f_t^{a_t}$ with $\sum a_k=e$ has some $a_k\ge e_k$, and these monomials generate $I^e$, so $I^ex=0$. Hence $K$ and $Q$ are $I$-power torsion. Increase any zero exponent by one, using containment of higher ideal powers, to obtain a positive exponent for the stated cokernel condition. If the chart family is empty, I=0 and exponent one suffices.

(Part (2): $\Psi'$ is injective.) Let $y\in K$. Then $y\in(H\otimes_RS)[I^\infty]$ (step 2), and since $I=(f_1,\dots,f_t)$ is finitely generated, $\varphi$ is flat and $R/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism, there is $h\in H[I^\infty]$ with $h\otimes1=y$ [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-submodule-flat-base-change-iso]. Then $p'(h)=\Psi'(h\otimes1)=0$. If $I^nh=0$ then $f_i^nh=0$, so $h/1=0$ in $H_{f_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] and $p_i(h)=\Psi_i(h/1)=0$ for every $i$. As $h=(p'(h),(p_i(h))_i)$ in $M'\times\prod_iM_i$, $h=0$ and $y=0$. So $K=0$. (The source argues with $H^0((K,0,0,0))=K$, left exactness of $H^0$ and bijectivity of $H^0(\Psi)$; the computation here is that argument written out.)

theorem exists_injective_approximation {R : Type u} {S : Type v}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) (t : ℕ) (f : Fin t → R)
    (Can : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R ⥤ Data.{u, v, max u v w} φ f)
    (hobj : (∀ M : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R,
        (Can.obj M).M' = extend φ M ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, (Can.obj M).M i =
          ModuleCat.of (Localization.Away (f i)) (LocalizedModule.Away (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha i).toLinearMap (compare φ (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i j : Fin t,
          HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha_overlap i j).toLinearMap (swap (f i) (f j) M))))
    (hflat : φ.Flat)
    (hquot : Function.Bijective
      (Ideal.quotientMap ((Ideal.span (Set.range f)).map φ) φ Ideal.le_comap_map))
    (X : Data.{u, v, max u v w} φ f) :
    ∃ (H : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) (ψ : Can.obj H ⟶ X),
      Function.Injective ψ.prime ∧ (∀ i, Function.Bijective (ψ.chart i)) ∧
      ∀ x : restrict φ (ModuleCat.of S (X.M' ⧸ LinearMap.range ψ.prime)),
        ∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧ ∀ r ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) ^ n, r • x = 0
